content_of_post_to_comment:
Hi, I’m 24F, and I graduated from college about six months ago. The first few months after graduation were really stressful for me because I kept getting rejected from job applications.

I don’t have parents, and my uncle was the only person supporting me financially, so I felt really guilty because I know supporting me isn’t his responsibility. I was doing everything I could to find a job, and after about five months, I finally got one that pays well. I’m really grateful for it, especially because I can now start paying off my debts and become more financially independent.

The problem is that it’s a work-from-home job, and I’m struggling a lot with self-discipline and having a proper routine.

Even before getting the job, my sleep schedule was already bad. I would sleep around 2–3 AM and wake up late. When I first started working, I was really slow with some tasks, and even though I’m supposed to work 8 hours a day, I would sometimes work extra hours because I wanted to finish whatever task I was working on. I still only charge for the 8 hours, but I kept pushing myself to finish everything.

Eventually, I started sleeping at 4–5 AM, waking up late, working late, and repeating the cycle.

Now it’s been weeks where I barely have time for anything outside of work. My house needs cleaning, I have chores and groceries to do, and I feel like I have no time for myself anymore.

I don’t have weekends completely off either. I work less on weekends, but I still have some work to do.
Today was the first time I genuinely felt like I had no energy or motivation to do anything, even work. And I think that’s when I realized I really need to change something before I completely burn myself out.

I keep thinking that if I could just fix my sleep schedule, wake up earlier, and have a proper routine, I would have so much more time during the day. But I’ve been struggling to actually make that happen.

For people who work from home, especially those who live alone or basically have to rely on themselves for structure and accountability, how do you stay disciplined?

How do you separate work from your personal life, make yourself stop working, maintain your chores, and still have time for yourself?

I’d really appreciate any practical advice, routines, or things that actually worked for you. I really want to get out of this cycle.
